location.altitude: 600–900 m (one of the highest-elevation tea plots in Wuyishan)

description.short: Rare high-altitude rock oolong boasting a dense, warm-spiced character and penetrating stony minerality
description.overview: Perched upon one of the most perilous cliff ledges in Wuyishan overlooking narrow ravines, its precarious location midway up the precipitous peaks inspired its poetic name ('Mid-Sky Demon' / 'Halfway up the Sky').
description.leaf: Dark brown, twisted leaves with charcoal sheen
description.aroma: Warmly spiced, stony and mineral, touched by honeyed sweetness and gentle roasted smoke
description.taste: Full-bodied, spicy, and fiercely mineral, characteristic of extreme high-cliff terroir
description.processing: Classic Yancha processing, hand-plucked from near-inaccessible sheer cliff terraces

history.origin: According to myth, an eagle dropped a tea seed on an unreachable cliff shelf midway up the heavens, where a spirit or demon guarded the miraculous tea bush.
history.development: Due to the perilous cliffs of Guidong (Ghost Cave), harvesting was historically strictly limited, granting the tea a mythical aura among monks and scholars.
history.modern: Today, Ban Tian Yao is esteemed among the celebrated 'Famous Cultivars' (Ming Cong) of Wuyishan, revered by purists for its dramatic cliffside origin and untamed character.
interestingFacts: Because it grows on near-vertical rock faces, harvesting historically required ropes, pulleys, and specialized ladders to access the ledges.
Widely recognized as having one of the most intense, unvarnished mineral profiles in all of Wuyishan thanks to the extreme cliffside terroir.
